extracted.intended_audience: FERC commissioners, regulators, utilities, energy market stakeholders, and antitrust/competition policy community
extracted.subtask_description: Notice-of-comment / advocacy summary responding to FERC's NOPR on refinements to horizontal market power analysis for sellers seeking market-based rate authority, arguing to retain market power screens and oversight. The page summarizes joint comments filed by AAI, APPA, and NRECA and their recommended next steps for the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit horizontal market power "screens"
rubrics_metrics.description: Current regulation requires a public utility to submit horizontal market power 'screens' to the Commission as part of the horizontal market power analysis necessary to obtain or retain authority to sell wholesale energy, ancillary services, and capacity at market-based rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NOPR would eliminate the requirement, under certain circumstances, for public utilities to submit horizontal market power 'screens' to the Commission; the joint commenters oppose eliminating this requirement because it would remove a key component of the Commission's market-based rate framework and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing regulatory burden reduction with preservation of oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's NOPR frames its proposal as reducing the burden on market-based rate sellers while preserving appropriate Commission oversight of its market-based rate program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAI, APPA, and NRECA argue the NOPR does not strike a proper balance: alleviating regulatory burdens should not come at the expense of guarding against harmful effects of market power in wholesale electricity markets. Eliminating requirements would 'further distance the Commission from oversight of the competitive issues' to the detriment of competition and consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of horizontal market power analyses to Commission and public
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizontal market power analyses provide valuable information to the Commission and the public concerning the possession and potential exercise of market power by public utilities with market-based rate authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joint comments stress that these analyses are informationally important and that both the Commission and the courts have long emphasized their important role in the market-based rate framework; removing them would reduce transparency and analytical basis for oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of impacts on competition and consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to market-based rate requirements should be evaluated for adverse implications for competition and consumers in wholesale electricity markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joint comments explicitly address the 'adverse implications of the Commission’s proposals for competition and consumers' and urge that proposals that risk harming competition or consumers be rejected or rethought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Commission oversight of market-based rate program
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory changes should not unduly distance the Commission from oversight of competitive issues in organized wholesale electricity markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAI's President warned that eliminating FERC’s requirements would 'further distance the Commission from oversight of the competitive issues that arise in the organized wholesale electricity markets, to the detriment of competition and consumers.' The guidance implies maintaining mechanisms (like screens) that enable active oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit public comment in future rulemaking before reassessing competition analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Before undertaking any further reassessment of the competition analysis required to support grants of market-based rate authority, the Commission should solicit public comment in a future rulemaking, particularly concerning RTO and ISO markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joint comments recommend that the Commission consider soliciting public comment in a future rulemaking so that information gathered could 'improve the quality and consistency of the Commission’s analysis of market power across the many areas where the Commission exercises authority to promote competition and protect consumers.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Special attention to RTO and ISO market contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reassessment of competition analysis and possible exemptions should account for particular conditions in Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) and Independent System Operator (ISO) markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commenters highlight that reassessment in these organized market areas is especially important and that tailored consideration could lead to better-quality, more consistent Commission analyses across jurisdictions.
